newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline called higher on bullish stock data.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline called higher on bullish stock data.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline prices were expected to open strongly Wednesday following the release of weekly oil inventory data which showed a surprisingly large draw in gasoline stocks.
Gasoline was seen opening 0.50 to 0.75 cent a gallon higher while crude was called up 10 to 15 cents a barrel higher. Heating oil was called up 0.25 to 0.50 cent a gallon.
"The stock data is bullish with gasoline inventories down and refinery runs up a healthy amount," said Refco Inc vice president Victor Yu.
"Gasoline stocks are down 13.2 million barrels compared with a year ago, and we may be up in crude (stocks), but we are using the stuff with higher runs," said a New York crude dealer.
The American Petroleum Institute (API) said Tuesday evening that gasoline stocks dropped 3.6 million barrels for the week ended May 2.

The stock data yielded an implied demand figure for gasoline of 8.7 million barrels per day (bpd) which dealers said was a near record, and made them skeptical of the data since they said it is still too early in the driving season to get such high demand.
"I don't believe the implied demand figure, and I think it's a function of the fact inventories are so lean, so demand drawn from the numbers will be more volatile," said a New York dealer.

But, Wednesday morning, the U.S. Department of Energy's (DOE) Energy Information Administration (EIA) confirmed the API data by showing a draw in gasoline stocks of 2.4 million barrels in its own inventory data for the May 2 week.
The EIA also said runs were up strongly, indicating strong gasoline demand offset higher production to create a draw.

In fact, implied gasoline demand has been above a strong eight million bpd in the past two weeks of API data, and traders had been expecting the May 2 API data to show an increase in gasoline stocks of one to two million barrels since they anticipated demand would ease.
Meanwhile, the API data said crude stocks rose one million barrels, in line with expectations, while distillate stocks rose 2.7 million barrels, making the data less bullish for heating oil.
Dealers had expected unseasonably cool weather in the key heating oil market of the U.S. Northeast to have decreased distillate stocks which are composed of heating oil and distillate.
